correctness.rationale: For any two permitted per-capita homogeneous degrees p<q, t=average(x) and phi_0=(q t^p−p t^q)/(q−p) has value 1 and zero gradient at x=1; phi_j=(x_j−t)t^(p−1)+(t^q−t^p)/(q−p) has value 0 and gradient e_j. Each uses exactly allowed degree p and q. Choosing H_i=−b_i phi_0+sum_j(−λδ_ij−S_ij)phi_j cancels arbitrary prescribed r,S at x=1 and gives full Jacobian −λI. Conversely for r_i=S_ij=−1 and a single homogeneous degree m≥2, any hypothetical positive equilibrium x* has H_i(x*)=1+T where T=sum x*_j. Along invariant positive ray c x*, c′=c[−1−Tc+(1+T)c^m]. This has derivative at 1 equal to m+(m−1)T>0, hence instability, and upper trajectories escape in finite time due dominant c^(m+1). Empty support has no equilibrium. Algebraic jet and radial identities independently checked by symbolic exact arithmetic for representative n,p,q; proof covers all n,m analytically.
